newsitem.title: UK: London gold drags feet, PGMs edge lower in PM.
newsitem.headline: London gold drags feet, PGMs edge lower in PM.

text.p: The gold market slumbered on Monday while platinum and palladium ticked marginally lower on light New York-led selling, dealers said.
Spot gold prices were lodged in a tiny range spanning less than $2.00 and dealers said business was slow with many players attending the Financial Times annual gold conference in Prague.
Bullion was fixed at $341.50 an ounce, compared to $340.95 in the morning and $341.40 on Friday afternoon.
The market has ignored a potentially bearish U.S. Federal Reserve study which that the United States and other governments should sell gold reserves to benefit their economies.
But the French central bank official told the FT conference on Monday that several central banks which had sold gold from reserves now see no advantage in selling more bullion.
Merrill Lynch analyst Ted Arnold said at the conference that the world gold prices was more likely to fall to $250 an ounce within the next 24 months than climb to $450.00.
Showing a little more movement, the platinum group metals (PGMs) drifted lower as light volume selling emerged on New York's Nymex futures market, dealers said.
"There's been some selling on the Nymex floor and that's reflected in the spot price," one dealer said.
"But volumes have been light from what we've seen," he added.

Platinum eased to $425.00/430.00, a decline of $12 from Friday's close. Technical analysts said platinum probably needed to correct lower after shooting to seven-year highs earlier this month, and could ease back to around $400 an ounce.
Palladium was similarly easier, although the market reluctant to stray from the psychological $200 an ounce level.
Prices were last quoted at $197.00/$202.00, down $5.
The market was still extremely tight due to long delays from key producer Russia and a suspected squeeze by U.S. hedge funds.
Some lending was seen, although short-term lease rates were still very high pending renewed Russian exports.
"There is more metal available than last week," a dealer said, putting one-month lease rates at 75 percent for platinum and 100 percent for palladium.

Dealers were closely watching for fresh news of the U.S. based Tiger Management hedge fund, which is believed to hold vast amounts of palladium. Dealers said the fund had tried to persuade Japanese trade houses to buy supplies last week.
Silver was quoted down one cent at $4.71/4.73.
